In local SEO for service businesses, the main risk of a programmatic approach is not page generation itself. The risk is that generation replaces the evidence base and produces pages that look architecturally clean but do not substantively deserve indexation.

- An interesting model is to let programmatic pages pass through gates: real demand, actual work performed in the region, sufficient unique material, freshness, and alignment with the maintenance budget. What matters is not the list of criteria itself, but the system’s right to say: this page should not become indexable yet. For local SEO, this is healthier than mechanically covering every city and every service combination.

- The semantic layer is useful when it is embedded into the build: Service, Organization, BreadcrumbList, FAQPage, and other entities are generated from the site structure. This reduces discrepancies between visible content and machine-readable description. But structured data does not compensate for a weak page. It only makes what is already there easier to understand.

- A local landing page and doorway logic should be separated. If a business has no actual presence, work performed, cases, regional context, or demand-specific characteristics, the page becomes an administrative fiction. A search engine may assess this differently than the author of the structure. That is why the “do not publish” gate is more important than the “create” gate.

What minimum set of evidence do you consider sufficient for an indexable local service page?
